title: County of Aragon
capsule: The County of Aragon was a small Pyrenean march centred on Jaca in the upper Aragón river valley, originally a Carolingian creation to guard the mountain passes but increasingly drawn into the orbit of the Kingdom of Pamplona as Frankish power receded. Through the 9th century the comital line of the Galíndez held the county largely as vassals of Pamplona: Galindo Aznárez I recovered Aragon in 844 only by accepting Pamplonese suzerainty, and his successors Aznar Galíndez II (867–893) and Galindo Aznárez II (893–922) ruled as the last autonomous counts. When Galindo Aznárez II died in 922 without a legitimate male heir, the county passed under the direct control of the Navarrese crown, retaining a distinct administration as the 'land of the Aragonese lords.'
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The county's existence and rulers are documented in Carolingian and Navarrese royal charters, but its precise territorial boundaries in the Pyrenean highlands are reconstructed from later ecclesiastical records and remain approximate.
